thread:
maggie (PM): ok team, quick sync  we need a lightweight tiebreaker rubric for slicing features into MVP vs v1. customers pushing for more surface but we can't slip the launch. proposing a 4-step rule: 1) customer-critical (blocking contract), 2) core success metric lift, 3) engineering delta <= 2 sprint weeks, 4) UX sanity. thoughts?

liam (eng): +1 for a simple ordered checklist. can we add an override path for security/regulatory asks? those shouldn't be tiebroken into v1.

sara (product-ops): agree, and suggest we weight customer-critical by number of affected tenants + revenue impact. also include rollback cost as a quick filter.

kayla (design): UX sanity is fuzzy  can we define "sanity" as: user can complete flow without fallback, and no new onboarding required? otherwise it's v1.

ravi (infra): from infra's view, anything that requires infra schema changes or new persistent cache layers should default to v1 unless committed infra time is in plan. that's a high risk.

maggie (PM): good points. here's a proposed short-form tiebreaker rubric we can apply in triage threads: 

1) Contract/Compliance blocker -> MVP only if contract forces it.
2) Core metric delta >= 8% (or X% depending on metric) -> MVP.
3) Engineering delta <= 10 dev-days across owners -> MVP.
4) UX sanity (complete flow, no extra onboarding) -> MVP.
5) Infra touch (schema/cache/ops) -> V1 unless mitigations planned.
6) Customer count or strategic partner (top 3 customers) -> push toward MVP.

liam (eng): can we convert "engineering delta" into a checklist: a) data migrations? b) new infra services? c) cross-team deps? each adds a modifier that pulls to v1.

maggie (PM): yes. let's use a quick scoring hack: start at 0, +5 for contract, +4 for core metric, +2 for small eng delta, -3 for infra touch, +3 for strategic customer. threshold >=6 -> MVP. simple math.

kayla (design): love the scoring thing  helps unblock debates. will create a one-pager with examples (signup flow, embeddings cache, SSO edge case).

sara (product-ops): propose we add a process: 1) owner posts feature card with rubric scores, 2) product triage meets twice this week to adjudicate ties, 3) PMs sign off for final cutlist. saves us the infinite Slack bikeshed.

liam (eng): for transparency, include an "engineering-assumption" field on the card with this format: ```
- risk: low/med/high
- infra-touch: yes/no
- rough-dev-days: N
- rollback-cost: low/med/high
```

ravi (infra): sounds good. also flag anything that requires infra deploy window or DB migration  those are blockers for MVP unless we can parallelize.

maggie (PM): next steps: kayla will draft the one-pager + example cards by EOD tomorrow, liam will add the engineering-assumption template to the feature card template, sara will schedule two short triage slots (30m) this week. I'll pilot the rubric on the top 6 candidate features and post results.

deploy-bot: deployment scheduled: prod-cutlist-review meeting created for 2024-04-12 15:00 UTC.

kayla (design): noted, will include a "demo/no-demo" marker so stakeholders can see impact quickly.

maggie (PM): if we hold to this, we should be able to avoid a timeline reset while being defensible to execs and customers. if any of you see edge cases where the scoring breaks, add them to the draft doc and we'll iterate. :thumbsup:

liam (eng): thanks  i'll try the rubric on the embeddings-cache proposal and post scores.

sara (product-ops): sounds good. we'll use this during the cut meeting tomorrow.

maggie (PM): thanks all  closing loop here.
